description: VM and container resource usage for Navio: host CPU, memory, disk and pressure; each container's memory against its limit; JVM memory fit; and per-service call rate and latency.

panels.description: Share of all vCPUs busy (everything except idle), averaged over the rate window.
panels.title: CPU used

panels.description: 1 - MemAvailable / MemTotal. Page cache the kernel can reclaim counts as available.
panels.title: Memory used

panels.description: MemAvailable: what new allocations can get before the kernel starts swapping or OOM-killing.
panels.title: Memory available

panels.description: Swap in use as a share of swap size. Occupancy alone is not a problem; see Swap activity for actual paging.
panels.title: Swap used

panels.description: Root filesystem, which also holds Docker images and volumes.
panels.title: Disk used /

panels.description: 5-minute load average divided by vCPU count. Above 1 means work is queueing for CPU or disk.
panels.title: Load per vCPU

panels.description: Processes the kernel OOM-killed on the VM in the selected range, inside or outside containers.
panels.title: Kernel OOM kills

panels.description: Time since the VM booted.
panels.title: VM uptime

panels.description: Busy vCPU share by mode, stacked. iowait means CPUs idle while waiting on disk.
panels.title: CPU by mode

panels.description: Used = MemTotal - MemAvailable. Available includes reclaimable page cache.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: Linux PSI: share of time at least one task was stalled waiting for CPU, memory or I/O. Sustained memory pressure means the VM is short of RAM even if nothing has been killed.
panels.title: Resource pressure

panels.description: Pages swapped in and out per second. Steady swap-in means working memory no longer fits in RAM.
panels.title: Swap activity

panels.description: Bytes read and written on physical disks (LVM devices excluded to avoid double counting).
panels.title: Disk I/O

panels.description: Current state of every container. Memory is the working set (what docker stats shows and what counts toward the OOM limit). Restarts count changes of the container start time in the selected range, including redeploys.
panels.title: Containers

panels.description: Working set as a share of each container's mem_limit. At 100% the kernel OOM-kills the container.
panels.title: Memory vs limit

panels.description: Working set per container, stacked: who is using the VM's RAM.
panels.title: Memory by container

panels.description: Working set as a share of mem_limit over time. Dashed lines at 75% and 90%.
panels.title: Memory % of limit

panels.description: CPU time used, in vCPU cores (1 = one core fully busy). No container has a CPU limit.
panels.title: CPU by container

panels.description: Bytes per second received (up) and sent (down). nginx carries all public traffic.
panels.title: Network by container

panels.description: Bytes written per second by each container's processes (volumes and writable layer). max() across devices because I/O is reported on both the LVM volume and the disk under it.
panels.title: Disk writes by container

panels.description: Bytes read per second by each container's processes.
panels.title: Disk reads by container

panels.description: The container limit must hold the whole JVM, not just the heap. Native = container memory minus heap and non-heap (thread stacks, GC structures, direct buffers). Max heap + non-heap above ~85% of the limit leaves little room for native memory before an OOM kill.
panels.title: JVM memory vs container limit

targets.expr: (max by (service) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service"}) and on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service"})) - on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",area="heap"}) - on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",area="nonheap"})

100 * (sum by (service) (jvm_memory_max_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",area="heap"}) + on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",area="nonheap"})) / on (service) (max by (service) (container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service"} > 0) and on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service"}))

panels.description: Container working set minus heap used. Steady growth here, with flat heap, points at a native or metaspace leak.
panels.title: Memory outside the heap

targets.expr: (max by (service) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service"}) and on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service"})) - on (service) sum by (service) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",area="heap"})

panels.description: Spring HTTP server requests over the selected time range, excluding /actuator probes. Calls between services are on the Service Graph dashboard.
panels.title: Calls by service

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (service) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",uri!~"/actuator.*",status=~"5.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (service) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",uri!~"/actuator.*"}[$__range]))) / sum by (service) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster",environment=~"$environment",service=~"$service",uri!~"/actuator.*"}[$__range]))

panels.description: Requests per second, excluding /actuator probes.
panels.title: Request rate by service

panels.description: 95th percentile response time. Dashed lines at 0.5 s and 1 s.
panels.title: p95 latency by service
